FOREWORD 



This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft fmalized by the Farm 
Implements and Machinery Sectional Conunittee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division 
Council. 

Dibbling board is a tool used in nursery beds for sowing seeds at equal intervals. In order to manufacture quality 
dibble board this standard has been prepared. 

In preparation of this standard assistance has been derived from Forest Research Institute* Dehra Dun. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
ob^erv^ or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded ofif in accordance with IS 2 : 
1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)*. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 



IS 14523 : 1998 



Indian Standard 



FORESTRY TOOLS — DIBBLING BOARD 

SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

This standard specifies the materials, dimensions and 
other requirements of the Dibbling Board used in 
nursery beds for sowing seeds at equal intervals. 

2 REFERENCES 

The Indian Standards as given below contain 
provisions which through reference in this text, 
constitute provision of this standard. At the time of 
publication, the editions indicated were valid. All 
standards are subject to revision and parties to 
agreements based on this standard are encouraged to 
investigate the possibility of applying the most recent 
editions of the standards indicated: 



IS No, 


Title 


2062 : 1992 


Steel for general structural purposes 




(fourth revision) 


2102 


General tolerances: Part 1 


(Parti): 1993 


Tolerances for linear and angular 




dimensions without individual 




tolerance indications (third 




revision) 



3 SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS 

3.1 The dimensions of the Dibbling Board shall be as 
shown in Fig. 1. 

3.2 The tolerances for various dimensions shall be of 
coai-se class specified in IS 2102 (Part 1). 

4 MATERIAL 

The dibbling board shall be made from commercial 
quality mild steel (see IS 2062). 

5 OtHER REQUIREMENTS 

5.1 The weight of dibbling board shall not exceed 
30 kg. 

5.2 The minimum distance of sowing shall be 
uniform. The sowing lines shall be straight. 

6 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 

6.1 All sharp corners shall be rounded off except the 
peg points. 

6.2 The dibbling board shall be free from defects such 
as cracks, rust, burrs and other manufacturing defects. 



t 






X25 ANGLE IRON 




All dimensions in millimetres- 

Fig. 1 Dibbling Board 



IS 14523 : 1998 



6J The dibbling board shall be given a 
rust-preventive coating and thereafter suitably painted. 

7 PERFORMANCE TEST 

The dibbling board shall be tested on a nursery bed for 
minimum of 25 setting. After the test the tips of pegs 
shall not show any sign of wear and tear. 

8 DESIGNATION 

The dibbling board shall be designated by the number 
of this Indian Standard as: 

Dibbling Board, IS 14523. 

9 MARKING AND PACKING 

9.1 Marking 

The dibbling board shall be clearly marked with the 
following information: 



a) Manufacturer's name and recognized trade- 
mark; and 

b) Batch or Code or Serial number. 

9.2 BIS Certification Marking 

Each dibbling board may also be marked with the 
Standard Mark. 

9.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the 
provisions of Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 
and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The 
details of conditions under which the licence for the 
use of Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers 
or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of 
Indian Standards. 

9.3 Packing 

The dibbling board shall be suitably packed as agreed 
to between the purchaser and the supplier to avoid 
damage in handling and transport. 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Aciy 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and 
attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form 
without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of 
implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. 
Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publication), BIS. 

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Suindards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latesHssuc 
of *BIS Handbook* and ^Standards Monthly Additions'.
